title: Bumpy Roads
subtitle: Rockslides are just the beginning of their problems.

trails.title: Temporary Product
trails.description: This product has not been field-tested in the "Storm." Handle with care.

content.text:
The Wearable Equilibrium Umbrella is a compact version of the standard Equilibrium Umbrella with the canopy removed. It retains the core Hofmann Knot structure, converter, and harmonizer, and is equipped with a waist-mounted nylon buckle—lightweight, durable, and secure against accidental loss. Designed for armed personnel operating in the "Storm," it reduces the burden of carrying a full umbrella while significantly improving combat mobility.

Please note the following precautions during use:
1. To ensure the stability of the Hofmann Knot, the device retains a glass casing to maintain optimal arcane conductivity. Although the casing has been specially reinforced, it cannot withstand heavy impacts. Avoid striking it with force or exposing it to sharp edges.
2. As development time was limited, the rain-shielding effectiveness of this canopy-free design remains unverified, and distribution has been limited accordingly. Each person must carry and wear their own unit at all times. Sharing a single device between two or more individuals risks insufficient coverage and may result in serious consequences.
3. Armed units are advised to request backup Wearable Equilibrium Umbrellas and a number of standard Equilibrium Umbrellas when submitting their application, in case of emergencies.

items.text: Bumpy Roads
Study Room, Library

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: That's everything I know.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you.
A map of the campus "on loan" from the library is laid out over the table.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The good news is most of the students are accounted for within the library, and it's secure for now. But, that's basically where the good news ends.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We haven't seen any signs of the instructors nor the school security. They may have retreated into the central watchtower, but if that's the case, I don't understand why they would send the children here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We've viewed what we can from the windows in the reading room. It seems impossible to reach the central watchtower safely.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The campus is crawling with Manus believers, and that's just the ones we can see. I doubt we could even make it as far as the central square.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: All four corner watchtowers are damaged, and I believe their Shelter Doves have been disabled.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: As for the library, it's only safe because the Dove in the central watchtower is still operational.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: So we just bunker down here and wait for reinforcements, right?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm afraid we can't. The central tower's immunity range is shrinking.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Unfortunately, if I'm correct, the library will be exposed before the "Storm" arrives.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Then we need to make our way to the central watchtower. But I'm not sure we have the strength to clear a path there.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: We can take advantage of the library's layout to hold the line for a little longer, but ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: If the major Dove's immunity range keeps shrinking, it won't make much difference.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: So, then, what do we do?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We wait.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The Foundation's reinforcements should be here any minute. They'll have brought enough Equilibrium Umbrellas for everyone.
Inside the Car
5 minutes earlier.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Hold on tight!
The speeding armored vehicle collides with the ground.

items.speaker: Paravyan & Lopera
items.text: Ah!
Its front lifts as it rises out of the pit like a ship cresting over a churning sea.
Even with their seat belts fastened tight, the impact jostles the occupants. As they regain composure, eyes shift to the winding mountain road ahead.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Why are these roads so bumpy?

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: What, haven't driven around here much yet? You'll get used to it. Rocks slide down off the mountain from time to time.

items.speaker: Paravyan
items.text: How far are we from the SPDM?

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Fifteen minutes, give or take.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: How did Manus Vindictae manage to infiltrate the school? Security didn't notice anything?

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Tsk. The guards there are only equipped with tranq guns. They wouldn't have been much use against the Manus.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: This isn't actually the first time they've attacked the SPDM.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: But this time they've sent an army instead of Olitiaus. Won't be quite so easy to deal with.
Lopera twists around to survey the convoy behind them.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: That won't be a problem. We're more than ready, aren't we?

items.speaker: Paravyan
items.text: Blackbird was at the school before the attack. Just when I thought she might get to take a break. I hope she's alright. Well, she's probably completely freaked out, but I hope she's safe, at least.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Quit your whinging, Beagle. Focus on the mission.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Our little birdie's gonna be just fine.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Is this Blackbird a friend of yours?

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Yeah. She might not think she's a soldier, but she's a survivor. If Antarctica and the Eastern Front couldn't kill her, she can handle a school.

items.speaker: Paravyan
items.text: But she's never really fought the Manus directly, has she? Only Critters and penguins in Antarctica. Oh, and then the rebels.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: The rebels?

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Ahem!

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: There's one thing you need to know, Beagle. Same thing I learned during her combat training—
*screech*

items.speaker: Paravyan & Lopera
items.text: Whoa!
The brakes squeal as Yermolai slams the armored car to a halt.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: What now?

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Captain signaled us to stop. Let me go check.
Mountain Road
First Squad captain's car is stopped a short distance ahead. Captain Osborn stands nearby, issuing commands over his communicator.

items.speaker: Captain Osborn
items.text: All units, pull over. Formation Y, stay alert. We have a situation.

items.speaker: Captain Osborn
items.text: Arcane Support, move up ahead.

items.speaker: Captain Osborn
items.text: All team, check your wearable Equilibrium Umbrellas. Make sure they're functional.
He hangs up and turns his attention to Yermolai. The Equilibrium Umbrella at his hip, fastened with a Hofmann Knot, is emitting a faint glow.

items.speaker: Captain Osborn
items.text: Did you notice?

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Yeah, and I double-checked too.
He gazes back over the rising hills surrounding them with intent.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: I'm not claiming to be an expert on these roads, but I can tell you one thing: We turned that same goddamn corner three minutes ago.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Right down to that daft rat-looking boulder.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Oh man! Think we could be trapped in a Maze Net?

items.speaker: Captain Osborn
items.text: Unlikely. A Maze Net couldn't cover a convoy so large.

items.speaker: Captain Osborn
items.text: Well, at least of the ones we've encountered before.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: *sigh* Hate wasting time with these arcane props.

items.speaker: Captain Osborn
items.text: Take it as a good sign.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Sorry?

items.speaker: Captain Osborn
items.text: If Manus Vindictae had the firepower, they wouldn't be trying to keep us distracted, which means we're a threat. They're trying to buy time.

items.speaker: Captain Osborn
items.text: Once Arcane Support decodes this arcane skill, or whatever it is ...

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: No, wait.
He raises his head to scan their surroundings again. It seems as if he's trying to sniff the danger out from thin air.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: That can't be right. Manus Vindictae's grown way more aggressive since the war in Europe. They wouldn't back down from a fight.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: If their only objective was to buy time, they would've set up closer to the school, somewhere they could reinforce quickly and keep us pinned down.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: So, why choose this spot? Looking around, this seems like a perfect place for ... a f**king ambush!

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Everyone, get back to your vehicles! Now!

items.speaker: Captain Osborn
items.text: *choke*

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Captain! Damn it!
He dives under an incoming incantation, using the momentum to roll toward the safety of his vehicle.

items.speaker: Paravyan
items.text: Yermolai, get in.
Yermolai wastes no time getting inside.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Enemies on the slope. Fall back.
Square, Committee Building
Despite the ongoing threats, the Foundation continues trudging through its Pre-Storm procedures as planned, but it has become obvious that their capacity is being stretched to its limits.
People are loitering outside the Committee Building, waiting for further direction. Two squadmates squeeze through the anxious crowd of refugees.

items.speaker: J
items.text: I'm gonna disagree with you there, "El Capitan."
J comes to an abrupt stop as they end their patrol. His voice drips with contempt, though it isn't directed at his superior.
"Razor" doesn't need to guess what's coming—another complaint from his newest recruit. As a captain, he has weathered them a thousand times and obliges with a sympathetic ear.

items.speaker: J
items.text: All those people out there ... makes me think of the folks that line up outside the soup kitchens, only there ain't any soup. No shelter either. Just a shove to send them on their way.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: The Foundation can only admit so many people.

items.speaker: J
items.text: So, what, they get to pick and choose who lives and who dies? We throw equality out of the window just because of the "Storm"?

items.speaker: J
items.text: I've tried to understand why my sister chose to join the Foundation, but what would she say if she saw this?

items.speaker: J
items.text: I can't shake the thought outta my head: those cold-hearted bastards sitting back in their glossy offices with comfy chairs, pretending to be philanthropists while they leave people to die.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Do me a favor, J. Do your complaining in private. I don't want to have to be the one pulling rank and charging you with insubordination.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Whatever. I know we can't help everyone, but you ain't convincing me that this is for the "greater good."

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: We ... What we're dealing with here is more complex than things back on Haight Street. I'm sure you remember.
The ring of his communicator rescues "Razor" from an imminent clash of organizational discipline and street philosophy.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Your shift's almost over, J. Why don't you go grab something in the lounge? Maybe have a chat with Todd.

items.speaker: J
items.text: You not coming with?

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: I've got new orders.
